title: Beyond the 956: Jesús de Miguel, CD Tenerife striker, dies at 30 after on-field collision
excerpt: CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel has died at 30 after suffering a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision during Monday's match against FC Andorra. The club confirmed his death on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel has died at 30 after suffering a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision during a match against FC Andorra.

CD Tenerife confirmed his death on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., in a statement shared by the club. De Miguel had been taken to the Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria in Tenerife, where he was admitted to intensive care after the incident on Monday, November 2.

“Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we announce the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m.,” the club said.

The collision happened in the closing minutes of stoppage time in the second-division match, which was tied 2-2, when de Miguel and FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono challenged for a loose ball. De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest, was treated on the field, and was transported to the hospital, where his neurological condition later deteriorated.

Born September 21, 1996, in Madrid, de Miguel built his career in Spain's lower divisions before joining CD Tenerife in the summer of 2025, where he became one of the team's attacking references.

The Spanish Football Federation postponed matches scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, as a mark of respect, and tributes poured in from across Spanish football, including LaLiga president Javier Tebas, who said he was deeply saddened by the death.

Spanish authorities have opened a routine investigation into the circumstances of the death, as is standard procedure for a non-natural death under Spanish law, according to Reuters.

Rest in Peace, Jesús de Miguel.

Sources: CD Tenerife statement; USA Today / Associated Press; Reuters via New York Post; Eurosport.
